summary: Argues high random volatility (Feb 2024) has broken intraday short-straddle systems: stop-loss jumps and thin liquidity in non-Nifty options caused big retail losses; best 'strategy' now is staying out; offers calendar-inversion alternatives.
lessons: Most important skill is knowing when NOT to be in the market.

Strategy viability depends on liquidity: Nifty absorbs many strategies; Sensex/midcap options lack offsetting flows.
In violent markets invert the calendar: long straddle current week + short straddle next week; in quiet markets reverse it.
Technical analysis stops working in very high volatility regimes.

title_clean: High Reward Trading Strategy in HDFC Bank & Bajaj Finance
summary: Covered-straddle playbook: hold stock/futures and sell ATM straddle monthly; illustrated with a friend's Bajaj Finance compounding story (2000→3500 with monthly straddles) and a live HDFC Bank setup (~25% expected in 6 weeks); averaging rules for quality non-scam stocks.
lessons: No strategy works by itself - it needs a market view; match strategy strength to conviction level.
Hold quality stock + sell ATM straddle monthly: premium income compounds a stagnant or slowly rising holding.
Pre-commit the three scenarios: below lower breakeven buy-and-average; sideways collect premium; above upper breakeven give delivery.
Only average down in quality companies hit by results, not scams; falling knives (SBI 400→50) punish averaging in weak names.
Quality stocks beaten by results/reputation recover, but steadily rather than V-shaped - which suits monthly premium selling.

lessons: Markets react to surprise, not to party: 2004 shock loss -30%, 2009 shock win +20%, expected wins 2014/2019 barely moved.
